analysis.one_liner: Hindalco is the Aditya Birla Group's aluminium and copper producer, and also owns Novelis, the world's largest recycler and roller of aluminium sheet for cars and drink cans.
analysis.whats_happening: Hindalco's board meets on 6 November 2026 to approve September-quarter (Q2 FY27) results, under two weeks away. The most recently reported quarter, Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026), saw consolidated net profit jump 75% YoY to ₹7,013 crore on record EBITDA across all four business segments, even after absorbing a ₹2,299 crore exceptional charge tied to the 2025 fire at Novelis' Oswego, New York plant. Separately, Hindalco terminated its USD 125 million AluChem acquisition on 1 October 2026 after closing delays, and the stock remains about 25% below its May 2026 peak.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of Hindalco as two businesses bolted together: a domestic aluminium/copper smelting operation that is currently earning very high margins, and Novelis, a US-based aluminium-rolling business that supplies carmakers and drink-can makers worldwide. Novelis had a serious fire at one plant in late 2025 that disrupted output and cost roughly $1.4 billion before insurance, with about $600 million expected to be a net loss after recoveries. The tension: reported profit is growing fast, but a chunk of that is commodity-price strength that can reverse, and the fire recovery isn't fully done yet.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue ₹84,825 crore (+32% YoY), EBITDA ₹14,989 crore (+73% YoY), net profit ₹7,013 crore (+75% YoY). All four segments - aluminium upstream, aluminium downstream, copper, and Novelis - posted their highest-ever quarterly EBITDA. Flag: the exceptional ₹2,299 crore Oswego fire-related charge is a genuine one-off, not an accounting artifact, and profit still grew strongly despite it, which says more about underlying momentum than the headline growth number alone. Novelis volumes fell 5% YoY (916 kt) due to the fire outage, but EBITDA/ton hit a record $265 (margin-led, not volume-led). Q2 FY27 numbers are due 6 November 2026; the prior comparable quarter's detail was not independently re-verified here.
analysis.performance_read: No recent demerger or bonus/rights issue complicates this stock's chart - the only corporate action on record is a 10:1 stock split back in 2005, which is already baked into the price series. The current 25.1% drawdown from the May 2026 peak of ₹1,143.73 is a genuine price decline (commodity softness plus fire-related costs), not a corporate-action illusion. Despite that drawdown, the stock has beaten the Nifty and peer Vedanta (VEDL) handily over longer horizons: +89% over 3 years versus Nifty's +18% and VEDL's +30%, and +87% over 5 years versus Nifty's +24% and VEDL's +39%. Over 1 year it's up 8.7% while both Nifty (-13%) and VEDL (-52%) fell.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates across sources cluster around 13x (ranging roughly 9.5x-15x depending on date and trailing/forward basis), with P/B near 1.5-1.6x - both below the metals-sector median (P/E ~19-25x, P/B ~1.9-2x). Why it looks cheap: ROE (~10-13%) and ROCE (~10-16%, sources vary) also sit below the industry median of roughly 16-19%, so part of the discount is earned - the market isn't just mispricing a quality business, it's pricing in weaker returns on capital than peers generate. Whether it is cheap depends on whether the Q1 FY27 margin surge (aluminium upstream EBITDA margins around 45% per recent quarters) is cyclical or durable; if it holds, the discount looks too wide.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is a mix: the domestic aluminium and copper businesses are growing on both volume and price/margin (downstream at all-time-high volumes, upstream margins near 45%), which is the more durable combination for a commodity business. Novelis, by contrast, is currently margin-led, not volume-led - shipments were roughly flat to down (941 kt and before that down 5% YoY to 916 kt because of the Oswego fire) while EBITDA per ton hit a record $265/ton (+49% YoY) on cost savings and product mix. That distinction matters: Novelis's profit growth right now is fire-recovery and cost-cutting, not demand growth.
analysis.health_read: Management says net leverage is being held below 2x EBITDA, and promoter pledging is zero, so financial risk looks contained on the numbers available. The bigger live risk is business/operational: the Oswego fire's cumulative cash impact has been about $1.4 billion gross, with $300 million of insurance recovered so far and a net loss impact of roughly $600 million expected, plus a recurring $70 million/quarter tariff drag with no stated end date. Whether operating cash flow is converting cleanly into free cash flow after these one-offs was not independently verified - check on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Aditya Birla Group) hold 34.66%, essentially flat for five straight quarters, with zero pledged shares - a clean governance signal. Institutional ownership is broad: FIIs ~31.4%, mutual funds ~10%, insurance ~6.8%, DIIs ~3.3%, retail ~9.6%. No single well-known individual investor shows up on the register in the sources checked - this is an institutionally-held stock, not one associated with a marquee retail investor.
strengths: Q1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹14,989 crore (+73% YoY) with record quarterly EBITDA across all four segments
Novelis EBITDA/ton hit a record $265, up 49% YoY, despite fire-hit volumes - evidence of real cost and mix discipline
Zero promoter pledge with promoter holding stable at ~34.66% for five consecutive quarters
Stock has outperformed both the Nifty and peer Vedanta over 3 years (+89% vs +18%/+30%) and 5 years (+87% vs +24%/+39%)
watchpoints: Stock is 25.1% below its ₹1,143.73 May 2026 peak and close to its 52-week low of ₹770.63, with Q2 FY27 results on 6 November 2026 as the next catalyst
Novelis's Oswego fire has cost roughly $1.4 billion gross (~$600 million net after insurance so far), and a $70 million/quarter tariff drag has no confirmed end date
ROE (~10-13%) and ROCE (~10-16%) trail the metals-sector median of ~16-19%, so the valuation discount reflects a real returns gap, not just sentiment
Hindalco walked away from its signed USD 125 million AluChem acquisition on 1 October 2026 citing closing delays - the reason for the delay wasn't detailed in available sources
analysis.one_thing: The 6 November 2026 Q2 FY27 results - specifically whether Novelis's Oswego-affected volumes have normalized and whether aluminium upstream margins hold - will show whether Q1's 73% EBITDA growth was a durable trend or a low-base, price-driven spike.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 results (₹7,013 crore profit, ₹84,825 crore revenue, ₹14,989 crore EBITDA) and the Oswego fire financial impact were cross-checked across IndiaInfoline, ApacNewsNetwork, Multibagg and a Hindalco earnings-call summary, and are consistent. Shareholding and zero-pledge figures were corroborated across Trendlyne, AnandRathi and Choice India. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, debt-to-equity) varied noticeably across AnandRathi, Dhan, Craytheon and MarketsMojo depending on measurement date and consolidated-vs-standalone basis - directional conclusion (cheaper than peers, lower returns than peers) held across sources, but exact figures were not reconciled to a single source. Operating cash flow conversion was not verified - check on Screener.
